title: Provenance-first promptset ACLs and canary eval rollback workflow
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Overview:
We need a provenance-first workflow for promptset (golden dataset) management that ties ACLs, immutable snapshots, and automated canary evals to config and model changes. The goal is to prevent silent quality regressions after model or runtime config updates by making promptset ownership, versioning, and permissions explicit and by baking canary/eval runs into the change pipeline.

Problem statement:
- Config or model rollouts occasionally introduce regressions that are only caught in production or by downstream customers.
- Promptset ownership/ACLs are inconsistent; engineers create ephemeral prompt bundles without clear stewardship or signed snapshots.
- Change gating is manual: there is no enforced canary eval that couples the exact promptset snapshot used during eval to the deployment artifact.

Proposal (high level):
1) Promptset manifest with provenance metadata: every golden promptset snapshot gets a manifest (SHA256) that includes steward, creation timestamp, dataset fingerprint, and an optional signer field. Manifests are immutable and stored in the artifacts bucket with content-addressed paths.
2) ACL inheritance and steward roles: implement a minimal ACL model (owner, steward, reviewer) for promptset artifacts. ACLs inherit from parent project unless explicitly overridden. Stewards are required when creating a production-level golden snapshot.
3) Canary eval orchestration: when a model or config change is proposed, CI triggers a canary eval run that references the manifest SHA of the golden promptset(s). The canary compares configured metrics (accuracy, hallucination rate, safety flags, latency) against golden baselines.
4) Automatic rollback/guardrail policy: if any metric exceeds a configured regression threshold (per-metric and global), the change is blocked and a rollback ticket is auto-created with links to the failing eval run and diffed outputs.
5) Auditability: every eval run, rollout, and ACL change emits structured events to the audit log with links to the manifest, PR, and signed approvals.

Implementation milestones:
- M1 (Design): promptset manifest schema + ACL model + canary eval spec (owner: Diego) — complete 2026-01-31
- M2 (Backend): storage paths, signed manifest write API, ACL enforcement hooks in prompt registry (owner: Priya Shah) — complete 2026-02-18
- M3 (CI/CD): integrate canary eval step into config/model rollout pipeline; store per-run artifacts and metrics (owner: Diego) — target 2026-03-05
- M4 (Console UX): steward assignment flow + manifest viewer + canary failure drill-down (owner: Lina Park) — target 2026-03-15
- M5 (Rollout): opt-in feature flag for teams followed by org-wide enforcement (owner: Platform Ops) — target 2026-03-22

Success metrics (SLOs for this feature):
- Mean time to detection for regressions caused by model/config change decreases to < 10 minutes in canary phase.
- Zero silent customer-facing regressions traced to model/config change in 90-day window for teams using enforced manifests.
- % of production rollouts gated by canary evals reaches 95% for dedicated/private customers within first quarter of rollout.

Acceptance criteria (for Done):
- Promptset manifest schema implemented and documented in Confluence with examples.
- Backend API to create and retrieve immutable manifests exists; content-addressed storage verified.
- ACL enforcement prevents promotion of an unsigned promptset into a protected rollout path.
- CI pipeline runs canary evals automatically and produces a summary dashboard entry with per-metric deltas and a pass/fail verdict.
- Auto-rollback tickets are created and linked when thresholds are exceeded.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Teams will find mandatory stewardship burdensome and create shadow flows. Mitigation: Provide self-serve steward assignment and lightweight approvals; allow temporary "sandbox" snapshots without enforcement.
- Risk: Canary eval false positives due to metric noise. Mitigation: Support configurable thresholds, smoothing windows, and per-prompt weightings; require steward acknowledgement for borderline failures.
- Risk: Attack surface from signed manifests/key compromise. Mitigation: Use KMS-based signing, rotation policy, and require 2-person approvals for changing trust roots.

Operational notes:
- Use existing eval harness (refs below) and expand to accept manifest SHA references so eval runs are reproducible.
- Add new Datadog dashboard for canary-eval summary and an incident runbook for escalations.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Provenance+Promptset+Manifests
- Draft PR for manifest schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3214
- Canary eval runner (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/tree/feature/provenance
- Example manifest (storage): s3://redwood-goldens/manifests/sha256:3b2a1f...
- Dashboard (Datadog): https://dd.redwood.ai/dashboard/abcd-canary-evals

Notes on scope: This ticket contains the core engineering lift to enforce manifests, ACLs, and CI gating. UX polish and org-wide rollout coordination are tracked in dependent PM tickets.
